answer: Here is one mechanism that works: score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because juniper only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. Concretely, atlas is enforced in the ledger: The network tolerates clones that do real work; it only refuses ones that add no signal. Any echo approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
